edits.reason: Removes the repeated structural-vs-blip resolution; replaces it with a Jamie voice beat that uses her 'small print' framing to arrive at the same sourced qualifier with more character.
Line 73 restates the private-lawsuit point already made at line 58; deletion removes repetition without losing any sourced fact or receipt.
Preserves the sourced FSB qualifier; adds Alex's callback to the synthetic-employee thread, earning the recurring bit and cutting one dead-weight confirmatory exchange.
Removes the RUFUS self-agreement artefact ('Indeed'); gives the closing a three-voice shape and a dry earned beat without inventing facts or forcing warmth.
Strapline duplicates the sign-off function of line 131 and interrupts the closing rhythm; deletion keeps navigation clean.

scenes.chemistry: Present but thin. The Rufus/Jamie 'interest coverage ratio' exchange (lines 22-24) lands and the cost-of-capital discovery at line 36-38 is warm. However most turns are one-sentence confirmations that don't push back on the previous speaker's actual claim.
scenes.discovery: Partial. Line 36 ('reshaping civilization… can they keep the lights on') is the payoff but arrives without the friction that should earn it. The question at line 28 resets rather than deepens.
scenes.repetition: Lines 31-35 re-ask and re-answer the structural-vs-blip question already handled at lines 17-20. The same 'we don't know yet' beat recurs.

scenes.chemistry: Stronger. Jamie's 'structural intervention' (line 53) and Rufus's 'fifty different versions of ChatGPT' exchange (lines 65-66) show real push-pull. Alex's admission at line 57 is a good character beat.
scenes.discovery: Good. Line 74 ('the new thing isn't the concern, the new thing is who's bringing it') is a clean, earned arrival. The Rufus imagined dispatch frames the multi-jurisdiction risk usefully.
scenes.repetition: Line 73 (private lawsuits already face) partially restates line 58 (dozens of private lawsuits). Minor but trimable.

scenes.chemistry: Best of the three. The 'synthetic employee' thread, the Hugging Face beat, and the listener-question callback at line 110 all build. Jamie's memo image at line 119 and Rufus's 'absence of a phrase' at line 120 are the episode's best exchange.
scenes.discovery: Strong. 'Regulation by deletion' (line 121) is a well-earned coined phrase. The spending-limit analogy makes the abstract trigger concept concrete.
scenes.repetition: Lines 95-96 (guidance vs implementation, FSB as recommendation body) partially duplicates the qualifier already given at line 89. The main structural point is well-covered by then.

scenes.chemistry: Thin. Line 126 ('Indeed') is a speaker talking to themselves — RUFUS follows his own line with a one-word affirmation. The three-bullet summary at line 124 is functional but flat; the friends disappear into a recap.
scenes.discovery: Missing. The closing doesn't land on a changed question or honest unresolved disagreement; it resolves too cleanly for what the episode earned.
scenes.repetition: Line 130 ('What changed. Who wins. What you do next.') is a strapline delivered mid-closing, duplicating the sign-off function of line 131.

review_before_repairs.rufus_feature: Segment 3, lines 62-64. The imagined scene is explicitly framed ('Picture this… a legal strategist in New York') and honestly acknowledges the multi-jurisdiction nature of the sourced story rather than claiming travel. The studio exchange follows immediately (lines 65-66, Jamie's pushback; line 66, Rufus's reply on building to the most restrictive standard). The feature is a genuine imagined scene with a grounded sourced argument, not merely a label. The return to the wider story is handled at line 67. Meets the brief, though the opening location caveat is slightly long.
remaining_issues: Segment 2 re-asks the structural-vs-blip question at line 31 after it was substantively answered at lines 17-20; the second pass adds no new position.
Line 126 is RUFUS responding to his own line 125 with 'Indeed' — a speaker agreeing with himself, which reads as a production artefact.
Segment 5 editorial closing loses the three friends' voices inside a summary bulletin; the warmth and unresolved texture the episode earned is not audible in the exit.
Jamie has three reactive beats but no comic beat across the full episode despite the brief specifying jamie_comic_beats as a tracked metric; her carried-away analogy trait is unused.
